issues.body: In `find_violations`, any non-empty inline value is accepted whenever the raw text contains the substring `workflows`. Thus `workflow_run: {workflows: []}` is treated as clean even though the filter is empty, and `workflow_run: {not_workflows: [CI]}` is treated as if it had the required key. Quoted strings/comments containing that word can similarly fool the check. This contradicts the script's stated guarantee of an explicit, non-empty `workflows:` filter and leaves exactly the silent configuration failure this gate is intended to prevent. None of the fixtures tests an inline mapping, so the defective branch is unverified.
issues.fix_hint: Parse the flow mapping structurally (including quoted values and comments) and apply the same populated-value validation used for block mappings. Add fixtures that reject `{workflows: []}` and a mapping with only a similarly named key, while accepting `{workflows: [CI], types: [completed]}`.
issues.title: Inline workflow_run mappings bypass the non-empty workflows requirement

verdict.summary: The new lint does not enforce its stated invariant for flow-style YAML. Its inline `workflow_run` handling only searches for the substring `workflows`, so empty filters and unrelated key names can pass. The self-test table does not exercise this branch, despite the workflow comment claiming each violation branch is covered. This creates a silent false-negative in the gating check it introduces.
